**Persistent cloud cover, heavy rainfall, and strong winds from Typhoon Dolphin are the dominant factors moderating Shanghai’s expected maximum temperature on August 11.** The storm made landfall along the eastern coast near Zhejiang province around August 9–10 and is forecast to bring torrential rain (potentially 200–400 mm in affected areas), widespread overcast skies, and gusty conditions through at least August 12. These conditions sharply reduce incoming solar radiation and enhance evaporative cooling, suppressing daytime highs relative to typical August climatology of 31–32 °C.

Numerical weather prediction models, including guidance referenced in recent China Meteorological Administration updates, currently indicate a most-likely daily maximum near 29–30 °C for August 11 amid ongoing thundershowers and high humidity. The market-implied probabilities—47.5 % for 30 °C and 35.5 % for 29 °C—reflect this consensus, with only modest odds assigned to 31 °C or higher because any partial clearing would still be limited by residual moisture and cloud decks. Lower outcomes (28 °C or below) remain possible if rainfall is heavier or more prolonged than currently modeled, but the primary driver remains the typhoon’s lingering influence on the regional thermodynamic environment. Updated model runs and official forecasts over the next 24–48 hours will be the key catalysts for any further shifts in trader positioning.
